lawyer:
Dr Rajiqur Rahman with Serajur Rahman with ABM Matiur Rahman, Advocates—For the Petitioner of both the Rules. 

Sheikh Muhammad Serajul Islam, Advocate—For the Opposite-Party of both the Rules.
parties:
Abdul Majid (Md) ---------- Defendant-Petitioner 
Vs. 
Md Emdadul Haque and another --------- Plaintiff-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
Both these Civil Revision Nos. 2175 of 2006 and 2176 of 2006 have been filed by the same petitioner against the same opposite parties (spouse) and on similar contentions. Issues to be decided are also substantially similar and common questions of law are involved in both these matters. Hence, both these matters have been taken up together for disposal by a single judgment.

2. Rules have been issued in both these matter calling upon the opposite party No. 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-4-2006 (decree signed on 4-5-2006), passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh, in Other Class Appeal No. 182 of 2003 and in Other Class Appeal No. 183 of 2003, allowing both the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-5-2003 (decree signed on 31-5-2003), passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Haluaghat, Mymensingh, in Other Class Suit No. 7 of 1999 and Other Class Suit No. 6 of 1999 (heard and disposed of together), should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Facts, relevant for disposal of both the Rules, in brief, are that, since there were 2 (two) deeds of exchange executed by and between the same petitioner, Ext. Ka and Ka( 1), and there are two separate opposite parties (who are husband and wife), therefore, two separate suits were filed by these two opposite parties (as plaintiff), being Other Class Suit No. 7 of 1999 filed (Md Emdadul Haque, plaintiff, versus Md Abdul Majid (defendant) and the Other Class Suit No. 6 of 1999, filed by Most. Sufia Begum, wife of Md Emdadul Haque, plaintiff versus Md Abdul Majid (defendant). I have gone through the pleadings of the parties, filed in these two suits, which are in the LCR. Hence, their cases are not reproduced here. It will suffice to record here that, by a deed of exchange No. 2751 dated 12-2-1995, the defendant Md Abdul Majid and Most. Sufia Begum, wife of Md Emdadul Haque have exchanged some properties (the subject matter of Other Class Suit No. 6 of 1999) and the property described in another exchange deed No. 2752 dated 12-2-1995, were exchanged by and between Md Emdadul Haque and the same defendant Md Abdul Majid (the subject matter of Other Class Suit No. 7 of 1999).

4. The party's case as regards their respective chain of title, in respect of the suit property, has been recorded in their respective pleadings and the parties have given depositions in support of their respective cases as well as proved their documents before the trial court, which were duly marked as exhibits, forming part of the LCR along with the depositions of PWs 1 to 7 and the depositions of DWs 1-6. These are also in the lower court's record.

5. Considering the aforesaid evidence and materials on record, the trial court had decreed both the suits, mainly on the finding that, both the deeds of exchange was executed by and between the parties (two plaintiffs and the same defendant) for proper consideration. The appellate court has heard both Other Class Appeal No. 182 of 2003 and Other Class Appeal No. 183 of 2003, simultaneously, and disposed of the same by allowing both the appeals and reversing the judgments and decrees of the trial court. I have gone through both the judgments and have taken notices of the issues framed and the reasons which these judgments are based on.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgments and decrees of the Appellate Court, the defendant-respondent-petitioner filed these applications under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rules.

7. Dr Rafiqur Rahman, Mr Serajur Rahman and Mr ABM Matiur Rahman, learned Advocates, appeared on behalf of the petitioner. Mr Rafiqur Rahman mainly submits that, the petitioner acquired 70 decimals of land in RS plot Nos. 38 and 39, out of which he has given 25 decimals of land from RS plot No. 38 and 5 decimals of land from RS plot No. 39, i.e. total 30 decimals of land to plaintiff Md Emdadul Haque and also gave another 40 decimals of land from RS plot No. 38 to Most. Sufia Begum, wife of Md Emdadul Haque. Hence, both the plaintiffs, have, in exchange thereof, transferred their lands, as mentioned in the schedules to the aforesaid 2 deeds of exchange, to the defendant-respondent-petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that, all the deeds of title of the defendant and other relevant documents were handed over by the defendant-petitioner to the plaintiffs-opposite parties for their examination and the plaintiffs were also aware of the defendant's possessions in 70 decimals of land given to them by the aforesaid 2 deeds of exchange, Ext 'Ka' and `Ka(1)'. He further submits that, there was no instance of concealment of title or possession, on the part of the defendant, as alleged by the plaintiff and that the said 2 deeds of exchange were done for good and lawful consideration as has been proved by the defendant, who has adduced oral and documentary evidences before the trial court. He next submits that the trial court has rightly dismissed the aforesaid two suits, but the appellate court has utterly failed to appreciate the evidence on record placed before it as well as it has committed grave error of law resulting in error in passing the impugned decisions, occasioning failure of justice, by holding that, the defendant had no perfect title in the suit property given to the plaintiff by the aforesaid 2 deeds of exchange, since the name of Jotindra Mohan Sarker has not been recorded in the SA khatian, therefore, the seller and all the previous sellers (via) of the defendant had derived no title in the concerned SA plots. The contention of the learned Advocate on this issue is that, mere omission of name of the original owner Jotindra Mohan Sarker in the SA khatian was not legally material to decide the title of the defendant or of the previous owners, who acquired title through Jotindra Mohan, inasmuch as the record of right is not a documents of title. Moreover, both the plaintiffs, being aware of the title and possession of the defendant in the property exchanged for, had exchanged their respective properties by executing 2 deeds of exchange and, by this time, the defendant, after deriving the property acquired by him through the said deeds of exchange, has already constructed his homestead on the property given to him in exchange and is living there with his family members. Therefore, he also submits that, in the given facts and circumstances, the findings of the appellate court amounts to misreading and non-reading of the facts and misinterpretation of law. He next submits that, khatian No. 103 of Mouza Kismot Norail records 60 decimals of lands in the name of Kasem Ali, from whom the defendant derived his title and possession in that 60 decimals of land. However, he has frankly admitted that this is an un-partitioned joint property of Kasem Ali, with other co-sharers. He lastly submits that, the impugned judgments of the appellate court are liable to be set aside and these Rules merit to be made absolute.

8. Learned Advocate Mr Sheikh Muhammad Serajul Islam has appeared on behalf of the opposite parties in both the maters. His main contention is that, the appellate court has properly assessed the evidence on record, facts and circumstances of these cases and has properly decided the issues of law and facts in the circumstances of these cases. He further submits that, the defendant has deliberately concealed the fact that, name of Jotindra Mohan Sarker was not recorded in SA khatian No. 223 and, as such, the defendant and his previous buyers (via), from which he claims to have derived title in the property exchanged, had no title in that property. He seriously argued that, the deeds of the defendant as well as the deed of the preceding buyers (via), who have claimed title with reference to the title of Jotindra Mohan Sarker, is absolutely defective, clouded and none of the previous buyers or the defendant had acquired any saleable title in the property transferred by the defendant. The defendant, he proceeds on, having suppressed the fact and having misled the plaintiff, had succeeded to deceive and obtain their consent in getting the two impugned deeds of exchange executed by the plaintiffs. He also submits that, a mere perusal of the impugned deeds of exchange, respectively marked as Ext. 1 and 1(Ka), will show that there is no specific schedule of the property, nor any boundary, which the defendant claims to have purchased and then transferred to the plaintiff in consideration of the property given to him by the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate points out that, transfer of property necessarily implies transfer of specific immovable property, which is lacking in these two deeds of exchange, so far as the 70 decimals of land claimed and purportedly exchanged by the defendant is concerned. Moreover, it is an admitted position that name of Jotindra Mohan Sarker does not appear in SA khatian No. 223 (Ext. 3) of Mouza Kismot Norail, PS Haluaghat, District Mymensingh, while names of Rajanikanta Saha, Sarat Chandra and Surendra Mohan Saha sons of Bhabani Proshad Saha have been recorded as 16 annas owners of land at SA plot Nos. 38 and 39 (which the defendant claims to have owed and transferred by the said two deeds of exchange). So, he submits, nothing was left in this 16 annas of land for Jotindra Mohan Sarker to transfer to anybody in the SA khatian No. 233 (Ext. 3) or in SA plot No. 38 and 39. Moreover, even the defendant himself did not take any step claiming or for declaration that, he is the title holder of 70 decimals of land at SA plot Nos. 38 and 39, nor he has taken any step to rectify or to open any mutation khatian or separation of jamabhagh in his name, pursuant to his title deed, nor he has paid any rent (Khajna) in respect of these 70 decimals of land. In these circumstances, he further submits, the finding of the appellate court that, the claim of the plaintiff side cannot be ruled out that Jotindra Mohan Sarker had no ownership over the property of plot No. 38 at the time of transferring to Kasem Ali on 27-12-1972, is very much based on admitted facts and document. Therefore, the learned Advocate concludes that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed no error of law and, as such, these Rules have no merit and the same are liable to be discharged.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials in the record.

10. I find that, the appellate court has properly assessed the evidence on record, facts and circumstances and the issues as well as it has independently assessed and decided the issues of law and facts, in the facts and circumstances of these cases.

11. Whether the defendant had deliberately concealed or not, the fact remains that, name of Jotindra Mohon Sarker was not recorded in SA khatian, No. 223 and that, the 16 (sixteen) annas of land in SA plot Nos. 38 and 39 (from which the defendant petitioner has purported to have transferred 70 decimals of land to the plaintiffs through the said two deeds of exchange) are recorded in the names of Rajanikanta Saha, Sarat Chandra and Surendra Mohan Saha sons of Bhabani Proshad Saha. Therefore, I find that, nothing beyond that 16 annas left for Jotindra Mohan Sarker, in the said property, to transfer to Kasem Ali or any other persons claiming Jotindra Mohan or Kasem Ali, by way of purchase or otherwise. The appellate court has, therefore, rightly found that, "It appears from the certified copy of the SA khatian No. 223 (Ext. 3) that the name of Jotindra Mohan Sarker was not recorded in SA khatian. Although Jotindra Mohan Sarker was one of the 4 purchasers on the strength of deed dated 21-3-1945 AD but his name was not recorded in SA khatian. Had Jotindra Mohan Sarker had any ownership over the property of plot No. 38 at the time of SA operation then his name would be included in the SA khatina No. 223 or any other khatian. As such, the claim of the plaintiff side cannot be ruled out that Jotindra Mohan Sarker had no ownership over the property of plot No. 38 at the time of transferring to Kasem Ali on 27-12-1972." This finding of the Appellate Court is very much based on admitted and proved facts and documents. Besides, the further findings of the appellate court to the effect that, " It appears from the evidence on record that, although Jotindra Mohan Sarker has sold out 50 decimal lands to Kasem Ali, but he had no visible ownership over that land as the SA record of the property was not prepared in his name. So, the title of Jotindra Mohan Sarker over the lands of plot No. 38 was defective and the transfer for 50 decimals land from plot No. 38 did not confer Kasem Ali any title over that property. Since the land of plot No. 38 was not recorded in the name of Jotindra Mohan Sarker then it is very natural that Jotindra Mohan Sarker had no ownership over the land of plot No. 38 at the time SA operation", are also based on the oral and documentary evidences as well as on the admitted facts.

12. 1, therefore, find that, the deed of the defendant as well as the deed of his preceding buyers (via), namely, Rajanikanta Saha, Sarat Chandra and Surendra Mohan Saha, who claimed to have derived title with reference to the title of Jotindra Motion Sarker and Kasem Ali is absolutely defective, clouded and neither of their deeds does confer any perfect title to the defendant or to his preceding buyers (via). The defendant even did not take any step, in such a situation, to get any declaration of title in respect of 70 decimals of land claimed and purportedly exchanged by him, with the plaintiffs, nor he has obtained any mutation khatian in his name, nor he has separated any Jama, nor he has paid any land development tax (khajna), nor he could mention any specific property in schedule to the disputed deeds of exchange, namely Ext. 1 and Ext. 1(Ka). I am also of the opinion that, the facts and circumstances of this case leads me to drawing an inference that the defendant, having suppressed these material facts and having mislead the plaintiffs, had succeeded to obtain their consent by practicing fraud in getting the two impugned deeds of exchange executed by them (the plaintiffs).

13. Besides, a mere perusal of the impugned deeds of exchange, marked as Ext. 1 and 1(Ka), shows that there is no specific boundary of the property which the defendant asserts to have acquired title by purchase and then transferred to the plaintiffs in consideration of the property transferred to him by the plaintiffs in the said two deeds of exchange.

14. The transfer of property necessarily implies transfer of title, interest and possession in an specific immovable property (identifiable with reference to plot number, khatian number, mouza, police station and district and specific boundary, which is lacking in these two deeds of exchange, namely Ext. 1 and 1(Ka), so far as the property of the defendant-respondent is concerned.

<u>15. The essence of the transfer of the immovable property is that, the property should be specific and identifiable with reference to the quantum of land, related khatian and plot number, Mouza, Police Station and District and having a specific boundary. In the absence of any specification of the property in the schedule of the said two deeds of exchange, the same does not confer, to the plaintiff-opposite party, any title and possession in any specific immovable property. Therefore, the disputed deeds of exchange are bound to fail and be scrapped for lack of any lawful consideration, disregard of the fact whether defendant has done anything on the property taken from the plaintiff in exchange of lands on which he has no clear title, which is not identifiable and for which he even did not pay any khajna.</u>

16. The fraudulent conduct of the defendant and his dishonesty are apparent from his previous and the subsequent conducts. Not only he abstained from getting his title declared or created any separate khatian and Jamabhag, he even did not pay any rent of the land purportedly exchanged by him as against the lands of the plaintiffs. So, all these illegalities shall be undone at the cost of the defendant within the time specified by the court of appeal.

17. Such type of deed of exchange without any specification and clear title in the property exchanged will lead to multiplicity of the proceeding, if this court encourages them and will cause serious hardship to the victim party.

18. Therefore, in passing the impugned judgments by the appellate court, it has committed no error of law, and as such, none of these Rules have any merit and the same are liable to be discharged.

19. In the result, both these Rules are hereby discharged.

20. The impugned judgment and decree dated 26-4-2006 (decree signed on 4-5-2006), passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal No. 182 of 2003 and Other Class Appeal No. 183 of 2003, are hereby upheld.

21. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

22. No costs.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Records be sent down to the concerned Courts at once.

End.
